Patrick Stewart changed genre acting forever with Captain Picard in "Star Trek" and Charles Xavier in "X-Men." 

""'Star Trek' was popular before 'The Next Generation' debuted, but it was not considered high art by any means. Stewart changed that. He brought years of experience from the Royal Shakespeare Company to the role of Captain Picard, turning the character into a universally recognized noble leader," writes Variety's Joe Otterson. "And many people point to stars like Robert Downey Jr. for shifting the perception around superhero movies, but Stewart was breaking new ground in that way as Charles Xavier more than two decades before the MCU came into existence."

REMEMBERING PATRICK STEWART

Patrick Stewart, the legendary actor best known for portraying Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in the “X-Men” films, has died at 86.

His family said in a statement: "We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia." 

"His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre.  He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise... He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role - in his art and life."

Heavy snowfall at Badimalika in Bajura district has left two young tourists missing after they lost contact while returning from the religious and tourist destination. The missing tourists have been identified as 20-year-old Manish Bohara from Bedkot Municipality and 21-year-old Sagar Karki from Krishnapur Municipality in Kanchanpur. They had travelled to Badimalika with a group of five people on October 26, while the other three members have already returned safely.

According to police, Manish went missing on Friday while returning from the Badimalika temple, located at an altitude of around 4,200 metres. Sagar was also out of contact from Friday night. Before losing contact, Sagar reportedly told police over the phone that his friend had gone missing and that he was stranded at Triveni Patan.

Heavy rainfall and snowfall in the high-altitude areas have made the situation more difficult, with both tourists possibly stranded in deep snow. Their mobile phones are currently switched off, and police are preparing to send a rescue team from Martadi to search for them.

Nepal Beats India, Pakistan and Bangladesh to Become South Asia’s Happiest Country

Nepal has emerged as South Asia’s highest-ranked country in the World Happiness Report 2026, securing 99th position among 147 countries with a happiness score of 5.147 out of 10. The ranking places Nepal ahead of Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, marking a notable achievement for the country in the global wellbeing assessment.

Finland has retained its position as the world’s happiest country for the ninth consecutive year, scoring 7.764. Iceland, Denmark, Costa Rica and Sweden followed in the top five, while Nordic countries once again dominated the rankings. The report is based on people's assessments of their overall quality of life, collected through the Gallup World Poll.

In South Asia, Pakistan ranked 104th, India 116th, Bangladesh 127th, Sri Lanka 134th and Afghanistan 147th, placing it at the bottom of the global list. Nepal’s leading regional position reflects its relatively stronger performance in areas such as social support and freedom to make life choices, although its overall score remains considerably lower than that of the world's happiest countries.

The report measures happiness through people's life evaluations and examines factors including income, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perceptions of corruption. While Nepal's regional ranking is encouraging, it does not mean the country is free from economic and social challenges. Improvements in employment, healthcare, education and governance remain essential to improving people's quality of life.

विभिन्न सञ्चारमाध्यमका पत्रकार पक्राउ परेको घटनाले प्रेस स्वतन्त्रता र प्रहरीको कार्यशैलीमाथि प्रश्न उठिरहेका बेला नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक (आईजीपी) दानबहादुर कार्कीले पत्रकारहरूबाट निष्पक्ष, तथ्यपूर्ण र साहसिक रिपोर्टिङको अपेक्षा गरेको बताएका छन्।

शनिबार सामाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमार्फत आफ्नो धारणा सार्वजनिक गर्दै आईजीपी कार्कीले नेपाल प्रहरीले सञ्चारकर्मीबाट सधैँ निष्पक्ष र तथ्यमा आधारित पत्रकारिताको अपेक्षा राख्ने बताएका हुन्।

उनले सञ्चारकर्ममा कुनै पनि प्रकारको बाधा नपुगोस् भन्ने विषयमा नेपाल प्रहरी हरसम्भव सहयोग गर्न प्रतिबद्ध रहेको पनि उल्लेख गरेका छन्।

कार्कीले विपद्को असर न्यूनीकरणका लागि सञ्चारमाध्यम र प्रहरीबीच अभूतपूर्व सहकार्य आवश्यक रहेको बताएका छन्। संवेदनशील परिस्थितिमा नागरिकलाई सही समयमा सही सूचना सम्प्रेषण गरी सम्भावित क्षति कम गर्न पत्रकारहरूको भूमिका महत्वपूर्ण हुने उनको भनाइ छ।

उनले विपद्बाट जनधनको सुरक्षा गर्नु नेपाल प्रहरीको मूल दायित्व भएको उल्लेख गर्दै यस कार्यमा प्रहरी सधैँझैँ सक्रिय रहने बताएका छन्।

विभिन्न सञ्चारगृहबाट पत्रकार पक्राउ परेको घटनाको २४ घण्टा नबित्दै आईजीपी कार्कीको यस्तो धारणा सार्वजनिक भएको हो। पत्रकार पक्राउ र समाचार कक्षमा प्रहरी प्रवेशको प्रयासपछि प्रहरीको कार्यशैली तथा प्रेस स्वतन्त्रताबारे व्यापक आलोचना भइरहेको छ।

लगातारको वर्षाका कारण त्रिवि क्रिकेट मैदानको अवस्था बिग्रिएपछि नेपाल प्रिमियर लिग (एनपिएल) अन्तर्गत आज शनिबार हुने दुवै खेल प्रभावित हुने सम्भावना बढेको छ। मैदानमा पानीको भेल पस्नुका साथै माटो र लेदो जम्मा भएपछि खेल निर्धारित समयमा सञ्चालन हुनेमा अन्योल देखिएको हो।

आज दिउँसो साढे १२ बजे लुम्बिनी लायन्स र चितवन राइनोजबीच प्रतिस्पर्धा हुँदैछ। यस्तै, साँझ ५ बजे विराटनगर किंग्स र सुदूरपश्चिम रोयल्सबीच अर्को खेल हुने तालिका छ।

तर, शुक्रबारदेखि काठमाडौंमा भइरहेको वर्षाका कारण त्रिवि क्रिकेट मैदानको पिच र आउटफिल्ड कभरले ढाकिएको छ। नेपाल क्रिकेट संघका उपाध्यक्ष रोशन सिंहका अनुसार वर्षाले मैदानको अवस्था बिगारेको छ। मैदानको मिडिया बक्स र भिआइपी बस्ने स्थानको बीचबाट पानीको भेल मैदानभित्र पसेको छ। पानीसँगै माटो र लेदोसमेत जम्मा भएको उनले बताएका छन्।

मौसम पूर्वानुमान महाशाखा र मौसमविद्हरूका पछिल्ला विवरणअनुसार आज बिहानदेखि दिउँसोसम्म काठमाडौंमा वर्षा हुने सम्भावना छ। यद्यपि, दिउँसोपछि मौसममा क्रमिक सुधार आउन सक्ने संकेत देखिएको छ।

वर्षा रोकिएपछि मैदानबाट कभर हटाएर पिच र आउटफिल्डको अवस्था निरीक्षण गरिनेछ। त्यसपछि मात्रै खेल सञ्चालन गर्न सकिने वा नसकिनेबारे निर्णय हुनेछ।

लगातारको वर्षाले आउटफिल्ड भिजेकाले खेलका लागि मैदान तयार पार्न समय लाग्न सक्छ। त्यसैले आजका दुवै खेल निर्धारित समयमै हुने सम्भावना कम देखिएको छ। मैदानको अवस्थाअनुसार खेलको समय परिवर्तन गर्ने वा रद्द गर्ने निर्णय लिइनेछ।

विभिन्न सञ्चारमाध्यमका पत्रकार पक्राउ परेको घटनापछि राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का सभापति रवि लामिछानेले पार्टीको सचिवालय बैठक बोलाएका छन्। समसामयिक राजनीतिक विषयमा छलफल गर्न शनिबार बिहान बैठक बस्न लागेको हो।

रास्वपाका प्रवक्ता जगदीश खरेलका अनुसार सभापति लामिछानेको अध्यक्षतामा बस्ने बैठक बिहान ११ बजे काठमाडौंको वनस्थलीस्थित पार्टीको केन्द्रीय कार्यालय घण्टीघरमा हुनेछ।

प्रहरीले पत्रकारहरूलाई पक्राउ गर्नुका साथै सञ्चारमाध्यमका कार्यालयमै पुगेर धरपकडको प्रयास गरेपछि यस विषयले राजनीतिक वृत्तमा समेत चर्चा पाएको छ। यही घटनाक्रमपछि सभापति लामिछानेले शुक्रबार राति नै पार्टीका नेताहरूलाई बैठकका लागि खबर पठाएका थिए।

बैठकमा पत्रकार पक्राउ प्रकरणलगायत समसामयिक विषयमा छलफल हुने प्रवक्ता खरेलले जानकारी दिएका छन्। तर, बैठकको विस्तृत कार्यसूची भने सार्वजनिक गरिएको छैन।

तीन पत्रकार पक्राउ परेको र काठमाडौंका विभिन्न सञ्चारमाध्यमका कार्यालयमा प्रहरी प्रवेश गर्ने प्रयास गरेको घटनामा व्यापक आलोचना भएपछि नेपाल प्रहरीले आफ्नो धारणा सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। प्रहरीले आफू प्रेस स्वतन्त्रता र पत्रकारको सुरक्षाप्रति प्रतिबद्ध रहेको बताउँदै पत्रकारहरूलाई पक्राउ गर्नुको सट्टा पछिल्लो समय प्रकाशित समाचारबारे छलफल गर्न बोलाइएको दाबी गरेको छ।

केन्द्रीय प्रहरी प्रवक्ता डीआईजी अविनारायण काफ्लेले सेतोपाटीसँग कुरा गर्दै सरकार र प्रहरी संगठनबीचको सम्बन्धबारे प्रकाशित समाचारका विषयमा पत्रकारहरूसँग छलफल गर्न खोजिएको बताएका छन्। उनका अनुसार केही समाचारले प्रहरीको व्यावसायिकता र अधिकृतहरूको कार्यसम्पादनप्रति अविश्वास सिर्जना गरेको तथा जनतामाझ नकारात्मक सन्देश प्रवाह गरेको प्रहरीको बुझाइ छ।

त्यस्ता समाचारले शान्ति सुरक्षा कायम गर्ने कार्यमा समेत असर पार्न सक्ने भन्दै साइबर ब्युरोले समाचारको तथ्य र त्यसको आधारबारे बुझ्न चाहेको काफ्लेले बताएका छन्।

यसअघि प्रहरीले नेपाल प्रेसको बानेश्वरस्थित कार्यालयबाट पत्रकार विश्वमणि सुवेदीलाई पक्राउ गरेको थियो। डीएनखबरका प्रधान सम्पादक धीरज बस्नेतलाई ईसेवा नम्बरसम्बन्धी विषयमा छलफल गर्ने भन्दै प्रहरी कार्यालय बोलाइएको र त्यसपछि नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको बताइएको छ। मोटिभेट न्युजका प्रधान सम्पादकलाई पनि प्रहरीले पक्राउ गरेको थियो।

त्यस्तै, नयाँ पत्रिकाको समाचार कक्षमा पुगेर पत्रकार नवराज मैनालीलाई खोज्ने तथा दियोपोस्टको कार्यालयमा सम्पादकहरूको खोजी गर्ने प्रयाससमेत भएको थियो। सञ्चारमाध्यमका कार्यालयमै प्रहरी पुगेपछि प्रहरी अधिकारको प्रयोग र प्रेस स्वतन्त्रतामाथि हस्तक्षेप भएको भन्दै विभिन्न क्षेत्रबाट आलोचना भएको थियो।

घटनाले विवाद चर्किएपछि प्रधानमन्त्री तथा मन्त्रिपरिषद् कार्यालयले पत्रकार पक्राउमा आफ्नो संलग्नता र पूर्वजानकारी नरहेको जनाएको थियो। प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहकी प्रेस विज्ञ दीपा दाहालले घटनाबारे जानकारी पाएलगत्तै प्रधानमन्त्रीले नियन्त्रणमा रहेका पत्रकारहरूलाई तत्काल रिहा गर्न निर्देशन दिएको बताएकी थिइन्।

प्रहरीले पक्राउ गरेका पत्रकारहरूलाई रिहा गरिसकेको छ। तर, समाचारबारे छलफल गर्न भन्दै पत्रकारहरूलाई किन पक्राउ गरियो र सञ्चारमाध्यमका समाचार कक्षमै प्रहरी किन पुग्यो भन्ने प्रश्न अझै उठिरहेको छ। घटनाले नेपालमा प्रेस स्वतन्त्रता, पत्रकारको सुरक्षा र प्रहरीको कार्यशैलीबारे गम्भीर बहस सिर्जना गरेको छ।

राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का संसदीय दलका सचेतक प्रकाशचन्द्र परियारले समाचारको विषयलाई लिएर पत्रकार पक्राउ गर्ने र सञ्चारमाध्यमका कार्यालयमै पुगेर धरपकडको प्रयास गर्ने प्रहरी शैलीप्रति कडा आपत्ति जनाएका छन्। उनले यस्तो गतिविधि तत्काल रोक्न र प्रेस स्वतन्त्रताको सम्मान गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरेका छन्।

शुक्रबार सामाजिक सञ्जाल फेसबुकमार्फत आफ्नो धारणा सार्वजनिक गर्दै परियारले पत्रकार विश्वमणि सुवेदी पक्राउ परेको घटना र नयाँ पत्रिकाको कार्यालयमा सादा पोसाकका प्रहरी पुगेको घटनाप्रति असन्तुष्टि जनाएका हुन्।

उनले प्रहरीको पछिल्लो कार्यशैलीलाई ‘पुलिस स्टेट’ अर्थात् ‘प्रहरी राज’ उन्मुख भएको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्। संविधानले सुनिश्चित गरेको प्रेस स्वतन्त्रताको संरक्षण र संवर्द्धन गर्नु राज्यको दायित्व भए पनि प्रहरीको यस्तो व्यवहार लोकतान्त्रिक राज्यको सामान्य चरित्रसँग मेल नखाने उनको भनाइ छ।

नयाँ पत्रिकाको कार्यालयमा पुगेका सादा पोसाकका प्रहरीको शैलीलाई ‘जंगे शैली’को संज्ञा दिँदै परियारले घटनालाई गम्भीर रूपमा लिनुपर्ने बताएका छन्।

उनले विदाको मुखमा भएको प्रहरी गतिविधिको छानबिन गर्न सरकारसँग विशेष मागसमेत गरेका छन्। साथै, पत्रकार तथा सञ्चारमाध्यमसँग सम्बन्धित विवाद र विषयलाई प्रहरीमार्फत नभई प्रेस काउन्सिलबाटै निरुपण गर्ने अभ्यास गर्नुपर्नेमा उनले जोड दिएका छन्।

परियारले प्रेस स्वतन्त्रताको सम्मान गर्दै सञ्चारमाध्यममाथि हुने प्रहरी हस्तक्षेप रोक्न सरकारको ध्यानाकर्षण गराएका छन्।

बङ्गालको खाडीमा विकसित चक्रवात ‘अर्नब’को अवशेष र पश्चिमी वायुको आंशिक प्रभावका कारण आज पनि देशका अधिकांश स्थानमा मौसम बदली रहने भएको छ। मौसम पूर्वानुमान महाशाखाका अनुसार कोशी, मधेस र बागमती प्रदेशका एक–दुई स्थानमा भारी वर्षा तथा हिमपातको सम्भावना रहेको छ।

हाल देशभर अधिकांश स्थानमा बादल लागेको छ। कोशी, मधेस, बागमती, गण्डकी र लुम्बिनी प्रदेशका धेरै स्थानमा मध्यम वर्षा भइरहेको छ भने कर्णाली र सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशका केही स्थानमा हल्का वर्षा भइरहेको महाशाखाले जनाएको छ।

आज दिउँसो कोशी, मधेस, बागमती, गण्डकी, लुम्बिनी र कर्णाली प्रदेशमा अधिकांश बदली रहनेछ। सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशमा भने सामान्यतया बादल लाग्ने पूर्वानुमान छ। कोशी, मधेस र बागमतीका धेरै स्थानमा तथा गण्डकीका केही स्थानमा चट्याङसहित मध्यम वर्षा हुन सक्नेछ।

त्यस्तै, लुम्बिनी, कर्णाली र सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशका हिमाली तथा पहाडी भूभागका केही स्थानमा पनि वर्षा र हिमपातको सम्भावना छ। विशेषगरी कोशी, मधेस र बागमती प्रदेशका एक–दुई स्थानमा भारी वर्षा तथा हिमपात हुन सक्ने महाशाखाले जनाएको छ।

आज राति पनि देशभर सामान्यतया बादल लाग्नेछ। हिमाली भूभागका थोरै स्थानमा मध्यम वर्षा र हिमपात हुन सक्नेछ भने कोशी र गण्डकी प्रदेशका पहाडी भूभागका एक–दुई स्थानमा हल्का वर्षाको सम्भावना रहेको छ।

आइतबार भने मौसममा क्रमिक सुधार आउने देखिएको छ। देशभर आंशिक बदली रहने र हिमाली तथा पहाडी भूभागका एक–दुई स्थानमा हल्का वर्षा तथा हिमपात हुन सक्ने महाशाखाको पूर्वानुमान छ।

चक्रवात ‘अर्नब’को अवशेष र पश्चिमी वायुको प्रभाव आज अपराह्नदेखि क्रमशः कमजोर हुँदै जाने महाशाखाले जनाएको छ।

विभिन्न सञ्चारमाध्यमका पत्रकारहरू पक्राउ परिरहेको घटनाबारे प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाहको सचिवालयले आफूलाई कुनै जानकारी नभएको दाबी गरेको छ। प्रधानमन्त्री, उनको सचिवालय र प्रधानमन्त्री तथा मन्त्रिपरिषद् कार्यालयको यस घटनामा कुनै संलग्नता नरहेको सचिवालयले स्पष्ट पारेको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्रीका प्रेस तथा अनुसन्धान विज्ञ दीपा दाहालले आज विकसित घटनाक्रमबारे प्रधानमन्त्री र उनको कार्यालयलाई कुनै जानकारी नभएको बताएकी हुन्। अनलाइनखबरसँग कुरा गर्दै उनले पत्रकार पक्राउ गर्ने घटनामा प्रधानमन्त्री तथा उनको सचिवालयको कुनै भूमिका नरहेको दाबी गरिन्।

यसैबीच प्रहरीले विभिन्न सञ्चारमाध्यमका समाचार कक्षमै प्रवेश गरेर पत्रकारहरूलाई पक्राउ गरिरहेको छ। शुक्रबार नेपाल प्रेसमा कार्यरत पत्रकार विश्वमणि सुवेदी, डीएनखबरका पत्रकार धीरज बस्नेत र मोटिभेट न्युजका पत्रकार शोभराज बराल पक्राउ परेका छन्।

त्यस्तै, नयाँ पत्रिकामा कार्यरत पत्रकार नवराज मैनालीलाई पक्राउ गर्न सादा पोसाकमा खटिएका प्रहरीहरू पत्रिकाको कार्यालयमै पुगेका छन्। उनीहरूले मैनालीलाई आफूसँगै नलगी कार्यालय नछाड्ने भन्दै समाचार कक्षमै बसेको समाचारमा उल्लेख छ।

एकपछि अर्को सञ्चारमाध्यमका पत्रकार पक्राउ परेपछि प्रेस स्वतन्त्रता र समाचारको स्रोत संरक्षणको विषयमा गम्भीर प्रश्न उठेको छ। तर, प्रधानमन्त्री सचिवालयले भने घटनाबारे कुनै जानकारी नभएको र आफ्नो संलग्नता नरहेको बताएको छ।

बंगालको खाडीमा विकसित चक्रवात ‘अर्नब’ र पश्चिमी वायुको प्रभावले नेपालका अधिकांश भूभागमा वर्षा भइरहेको छ। कोशीदेखि गण्डकी प्रदेशसम्म शुक्रबार बिहानैदेखि झरी परेको छ भने वर्षा विस्तार हुँदै सुदूरपश्चिमसम्म पुगेको छ। काठमाडौं उपत्यकामा पनि रातिदेखि पानी पर्ने र रोकिने क्रम जारी छ।

जल तथा मौसम विज्ञान विभागका अनुसार पछिल्लो १२ घण्टामा कोशी प्रदेशका केही स्थानमा भारी वर्षा मापन भएको छ। धनकुटाको लेगुवाघाटमा ५२.८ मिलिमिटर र खोटाङको कुर्लेघाटमा ४८.२ मिलिमिटर वर्षा भएको छ। मौसमविद् रोजन लामिछानेका अनुसार न्यूनचापीय प्रणाली नेपालतर्फ अझै नजिकिँदै रहेकाले साँझपछि वर्षाको क्रम थप बढ्न सक्छ। विशेषगरी कोशी र बागमती प्रदेशका हिमाली क्षेत्रमा बढी वर्षा हुने सम्भावना छ।

त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालयका सहप्राध्यापक डा. विनोद पोखरेलले चक्रवात ‘अर्नब’को प्रभावले करिब ५ देखि १० घण्टासम्म भारी वर्षा हुन सक्ने बताएका छन्। यद्यपि वर्षाको समय, स्थान र मात्रा परिवर्तन हुन सक्ने भएकाले उनले साँझ र रातिको समयमा सतर्क रहन तथा आधिकारिक मौसम सूचना नियमित रूपमा हेर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्।

जापानका लागि प्रस्तावित नेपाली राजदूत जिज्ञान कुमार थापाबारे निर्णय लिन संसदीय सुनुवाइ समितिको बैठक आगामी सोमबार दिउँसो ३ बजे सिंहदरबारमा बस्ने भएको छ। सुनुवाइका क्रममा उठेका प्रश्नको चित्तबुझ्दो जवाफ र जापान सरकारबाट आवश्यक विवरण प्राप्त नभएपछि समितिले यसअघि उनको नाम अनुमोदन गर्ने वा नगर्ने निर्णय स्थगित गरेको थियो।

थापाको जापानको स्थायी बसोबास अनुमतिपत्र (पीआर), परिवारको पीआर, जापानमा रहेको घर–सम्पत्ति तथा त्यहाँको सरकारी निकायसँगको सम्बन्धबारे प्रश्न उठेको थियो। थापाले आफूले जापानको पीआर त्यागिसकेको बताए पनि उनकी श्रीमतीको पीआर कायमै रहेको र उनको नाममा जापानमा घरसमेत रहेको स्वीकार गरेका थिए। यसले राजदूत नियुक्तिमा स्वार्थ बाझिन सक्ने भन्दै समितिमा उजुरीसमेत परेको थियो।

यस विषयमा स्पष्ट जानकारी माग्दै समितिले परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालयमार्फत जापान सरकारसँग विवरण मागेको छ। तर, हालसम्म जापान सरकारबाट जवाफ प्राप्त भएको छैन। समितिले परराष्ट्र मन्त्रालयको रायसमेत लिएर यही कात्तिक १९ गतेभित्र थापाबारे अन्तिम निर्णय गर्ने तयारी गरेको छ।

संविधान तथा संसदीय सुनुवाइसम्बन्धी नियमअनुसार प्रस्तावित राजदूतको नाम प्राप्त भएको ४५ दिनभित्र समितिले निर्णय गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था छ। कात्तिक १९ गते उक्त समयसीमा पूरा हुँदैछ। निर्धारित समयभित्र समितिले निर्णय दिन नसके थापाको नाम स्वतः अनुमोदन भएको मानिनेछ। त्यसैले सोमबारको बैठकलाई उनको राजदूत नियुक्तिको भविष्य निर्धारण गर्ने महत्वपूर्ण बैठकका रूपमा हेरिएको छ।

नेपाली क्रिकेटमा नयाँ प्रतिभाको उदय भइरहेका बेला रौतहटका १६ वर्षीय राहुल यादवले नेपाल प्रिमियर लिग (एनपिएल) मा आफ्नो क्षमता प्रभावशाली रूपमा प्रमाणित गरेका छन्। कक्षा ९ मा अध्ययनरत जनकपुर बोल्ट्सका युवा मध्यम गतिका बलर राहुलले बिहीबार काठमाडौं गोर्खाजविरुद्ध चार विकेट लिएपछि उनी चर्चामा आएका छन्।

कीर्तिपुरस्थित त्रिवि क्रिकेट मैदानमा भएको खेलमा राहुलले चार ओभर बलिङ गर्दै ३१ रन खर्चिएर चार महत्वपूर्ण विकेट लिए। उनले साम हेजलेट, स्मित पटेल, काठमाडौंका कप्तान करण केसी र मोहम्मद आदिल आलमलाई आउट गरे। उनको उत्कृष्ट बलिङका कारण काठमाडौंको ब्याटिङ दबाबमा परेको थियो। काठमाडौंले दिएको ११६ रनको लक्ष्य जनकपुरले आठ विकेट बाँकी रहँदै पूरा गर्‍यो।

राहुलका लागि यो एनपिएलको दोस्रो खेल थियो। यसअघि कर्णाली याक्सविरुद्धको डेब्यू खेलमा उनले १५ रन खर्चेर दुई विकेट लिएका थिए। पहिलो खेलमा केही नर्भस भए पनि विकेट लिन सफल भएपछि आत्मविश्वास बढेको उनले बताएका छन्।

काठमाडौंविरुद्धको खेलपछि राहुलले पहिलो खेलको अनुभवले दोस्रो खेलमा राम्रो प्रदर्शन गर्न सहयोग गरेको बताए। “कर्णालीविरुद्धको पहिलो खेल एनपिएलमा मेरो पहिलो थियो। केही नर्भस थिएँ। पहिलो खेलमा विकेट लिन सफल भएपछि आज त्यो डर भाग्यो। त्यसैले आज विकेट लिन सफल भएँ,” उनले भने।

मधेश प्रदेशको रौतहटस्थित चन्द्रपुरका राहुलको क्रिकेट यात्रा खुला मैदानबाट सुरु भएको हो। चन्द्रपुर क्रिकेट एकेडेमीमा आफ्नो बलिङ कौशल निखारेका उनले कम उमेरमै बलिङको गति र क्षमताका कारण ध्यान आकर्षित गर्न थालेका थिए। उनका बुबाले क्रिकेट नबुझे पनि आफूलाई निरन्तर साथ र समर्थन दिँदै आएको राहुलले बताएका छन्।

जनकपुर बोल्ट्सले आयोजना गरेको ट्यालेन्ट हन्टबाट छनोट भएपछि उनी टोलीमा आइकोनिक खेलाडीका रूपमा आबद्ध भएका हुन्। स्थानीय स्तरबाट प्रतिभा पहिचान गर्ने प्रतियोगितामार्फत राष्ट्रिय स्तरको फ्रेन्चाइज लिगसम्म पुग्नु राहुलको क्रिकेट यात्राको महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धि बनेको छ।

एनपिएलअघि चन्द्रपुर क्रिकेट लिगमा पनि उनले राम्रो प्रदर्शन गरेका थिए। उक्त प्रतियोगितामा म्यान अफ द म्याच बनेका राहुलले एनपिएलमा समेत आफ्नो क्षमता देखाउने संकेत गरेका थिए। कर्णालीविरुद्ध दुई विकेट र त्यसपछि काठमाडौंविरुद्ध चार विकेट लिनुले उनको आत्मविश्वास र सम्भावनालाई थप उजागर गरेको छ।

कक्षा ९ को पढाइसँगै नेपाली क्रिकेटको ठूलो मञ्चमा आफ्नो प्रतिभा देखाइरहेका राहुलको प्रदर्शनले नयाँ पुस्ताका खेलाडीप्रति आशा जगाएको छ। १६ वर्षकै उमेरमा एनपिएलमा प्रभाव छाड्न सफल उनको यो सुरुवात आगामी क्रिकेट यात्राका लागि उत्साहजनक संकेत बनेको छ।

स्पेनको मध्य क्षेत्रमा भएको भीषण रेल दुर्घटनाले ६९ जनाको ज्यान लिएको छ। सयभन्दा बढी यात्रु घाइते भएका छन्। तर यो दुर्घटनाले ज्यान गुमाउनेमध्ये २४ वर्षीया युवा एथलेटिक्स खेलाडी जुलिएटा गालेगोको निधनले खेलकुद जगत्‌लाई विशेष रूपमा स्तब्ध बनाएको छ।

सानै उमेरमा खेलकुदमा आफ्नो पहिचान बनाउँदै भविष्यका लागि सपना सजाइरहेकी जुलिएटाको जीवनयात्रा रेल दुर्घटनासँगै अचानक समाप्त भएको छ। उनी म्याड्रिडस्थित एथलेटिक्स क्लब एडी स्प्रिन्टबाट लङ जम्प प्रतियोगितामा सहभागी हुँदै आएकी थिइन्। उनले आफ्नो उत्कृष्ट प्रदर्शनमा ५.९ मिटरको छलाङ लगाएकी थिइन्। तर अब उनको खेल मैदानमा फर्किने सपना कहिल्यै पूरा हुने छैन।

स्पेनको रोयल एथलेटिक्स महासंघले जुलिएटाको निधनप्रति गहिरो दुःख व्यक्त गर्दै उनलाई श्रद्धाञ्जली दिएको छ। महासंघले उनको निधनलाई एथलेटिक्स समुदायका लागि अपूरणीय क्षति भनेको छ। २४ वर्षको उमेरमै सम्भावनाले भरिएको जीवन गुमाउनु उनका परिवार, साथीभाइ र खेलकुद क्षेत्रका लागि असह्य पीडा बनेको छ।

बुधबार बिहान मध्य स्पेनको उर्दा नजिकै तीव्र गतिमा गुडिरहेको रेन्फे रेल र रोकिराखिएको इरियो रेल एउटै ट्र्याकमा ठोक्किएका थिए। भीषण ठक्करपछि रेलका कैयौँ डिब्बा लिकबाट बाहिरिएका थिए। दुर्घटनामा ६९ जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ भने सयभन्दा बढी घाइते भएका छन्। घाइतेमध्ये धेरैको अवस्था गम्भीर रहेको बताइएको छ। मृतकको संख्या अझै बढ्न सक्ने अधिकारीहरूले आशंका गरेका छन्।

दुर्घटनामा स्पेनकी पूर्वरोजगारमन्त्री फातिमा बानेज, ५९, सिभिल गार्डका अधिकारी जोसे म्यानुएल चाकोन, ३१, तथा वित्त र करसम्बन्धी वकिल एन्टोनियो मोन्तेरो डोमिङ्गेजले पनि ज्यान गुमाएका छन्। बानेजले सन् २०११ देखि २०१८ सम्म तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री मारियानो राखोयको सरकारमा रोजगारमन्त्रीका रूपमा काम गरेकी थिइन्। उनी उक्त मन्त्रालय सम्हाल्ने पहिलो महिला पनि थिइन्।

यता, आफन्त गुमाएका परिवारहरू अझै पनि आफ्ना प्रियजनको खोजीमा अस्पतालहरू धाइरहेका छन्। मृतकको पहिचान गर्न परिवारका सदस्यहरूले डीएनए नमुना उपलब्ध गराइरहेका छन्। कसैका लागि यो दुर्घटना जीवनसाथी गुमाउनुको पीडा बनेको छ, कसैका लागि सन्तान र आफन्त गुमाउनुको कहिल्यै निको नहुने घाउ।

सन् २०१३ पछिकै स्पेनको सबैभन्दा ठूलो रेल दुर्घटनाका रूपमा वर्णन गरिएको यस घटनाले पूरै देशलाई शोकमा डुबाएको छ। दुर्घटनामा ज्यान गुमाउने सबैप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्दै घाइतेहरूको शीघ्र स्वास्थ्यलाभको कामना गरिएको छ। तर जुलिएटा जस्ता युवाहरूको अधुरो सपना र उनीहरूलाई पर्खिरहेका परिवारको पीडा यो दुर्घटनाको सबैभन्दा मर्मस्पर्शी पक्ष बनेको छ।

यसैबीच नेपाली सेनाले आफ्नो व्यवस्थापनमा निर्माण भइरहेको काठमाडौं–तराई/मधेश द्रुतमार्गको कामलाई समेत तीव्रता दिने जनाएको छ। निर्माणमा देखिएका ढिलाइ र अन्य समस्या समाधान गर्दै आयोजना समयमै सम्पन्न गर्ने प्रयास भइरहेको सेनाको भनाइ छ।

फ्रान्स फुटबलले आयोजना गरेको B.O.A.T. (Ballon d’Or of All Time)नामक मतदानमा रोनाल्डोको सन् २००८ को ऐतिहासिक प्रदर्शनले सर्वाधिक समर्थन प्राप्त गरेको हो। अक्टोबर २८ मा सार्वजनिक अन्तिम नतिजाअनुसार रोनाल्डो पहिलो र अर्जेन्टिनी स्टार लियोनल मेस्सी दोस्रो स्थानमा रहेका छन्।

रोनाल्डोले सन् २००७/०८ को सिजनमा इंग्लिस क्लब म्यानचेस्टर युनाइटेडबाट खेल्दै ४२ गोल गरेका थिए। उनको उत्कृष्ट प्रदर्शनकै कारण म्यानचेस्टर युनाइटेडले इंग्लिस प्रिमियर लिग र युरोपियन च्याम्पियन्स लिगको उपाधि जितेको थियो।

त्यही ऐतिहासिक प्रदर्शनका आधारमा रोनाल्डोले सन् २००८ मा आफ्नो करियरको पहिलो बालोन डी’ओर जितेका थिए। अहिले समर्थकहरूको मतदानले उनको त्यही सिजनलाई इतिहासकै उत्कृष्ट बालोन डी’ओर विजेता सिजनका रूपमा छनोट गरेको हो।

यस विशेष मतदानमा मेस्सीको सन् २०१२ को प्रदर्शन दोस्रो स्थानमा रह्यो। मेस्सीले उक्त वर्ष क्लब र राष्ट्रिय टोलीका लागि कुल ९१ गोल गर्दै विश्व फुटबलमा कीर्तिमान बनाएका थिए।

त्यस्तै रोनाल्डोले रियल म्याड्रिडबाट खेल्दै सन् २०१७ मा जितेको बालोन डी’ओर तेस्रो स्थानमा रह्यो।

रोनाल्डोको उपलब्धिपछि पूर्वक्लब म्यानचेस्टर युनाइटेड र रियल म्याड्रिडले समेत उनलाई बधाई दिएका छन्। रियल म्याड्रिडले आधिकारिक वेबसाइटमार्फत उनको ऐतिहासिक उपलब्धिको प्रशंसा गरेको छ।

रोनाल्डोले आफ्नो करियरमा पाँचपटक नियमित बालोन डी’ओर जितेका छन् भने मेस्सीले आठपटक यो प्रतिष्ठित अवार्ड हात पारेका छन्।

तर यसपटकको सम्मान नियमित बालोन डी’ओर पुरस्कारभन्दा फरक हो। यो समर्थकहरूले अनलाइन मतदानबाट छनोट गरेको विशेष सम्मान हो। मतदानमा शुल्क तिरेर एकभन्दा बढी मत दिनसमेत सकिने व्यवस्था थियो। आयोजकका अनुसार यसका लागि छुट्टै भौतिक ट्रफी प्रदान गरिएको छैन।

मोरङको लेटाङका पदमबहादुर रायलाई मृत ठानेर परिवारले अन्त्येष्टि गरेको आठ महिनापछि उनी जीवितै घर फर्किएका छन्। उनको मृत्यु भएको विश्वासमा अन्त्येष्टि गरिएको व्यक्ति को थिए भन्ने प्रश्न भने अझै अनुत्तरित छ। घटनापछि प्रहरीले पुरानो दुर्घटनाको फाइल पुनः खोलेर अनुसन्धान थालेको छ।

लेटाङ नगरपालिका–५ खेरूवाका ३७ वर्षीय पदमबहादुरको मृत्यु भएको ठानेर परिवारले गत जेठ २७ गते अन्त्येष्टि गरेको थियो। उनको मृत्युका आधारमा परिवारले दुर्घटना बीमाबापत ५ लाख ५० हजार रुपैयाँसमेत प्राप्त गरेको थियो। तर, पदमबहादुर जीवितै फर्किएपछि शवको पहिचान र बीमा भुक्तानीको विषय फेरि अनुसन्धानको दायरामा आएको छ।

मोरङका प्रहरी प्रमुख एसपी कवित कटुवालका अनुसार परिवारले पदमबहादुर जीवितै रहेको पुष्टि गरेपछि प्रहरीले घटनासँग सम्बन्धित पुराना तस्बिर र भिडिओको अध्ययन थालेको छ।

‘उहाँ जीवितै फर्किएको कुरा परिवारले पुष्टि गर्नुभएपछि हामी फोटो–भिडिओ हेरेर पुनः अनुसन्धानमा जुटेका छौँ,’ कटुवालले बताएका छन्। परिवारले बीमाबापत प्राप्त रकम फिर्ता गर्ने बताएको र प्रहरीसँग समन्वय गरिरहेको पनि उनले जानकारी दिएका छन्।
दुर्घटनामा मृत्यु भएका व्यक्ति को थिए?
प्रहरीको अनुसन्धान अब मुख्यतः दुई प्रश्नमा केन्द्रित छ। पहिलो, दुर्घटनामा मृत्यु भएका व्यक्तिको वास्तविक पहिचान के थियो? दोस्रो, परिवारले उक्त शवलाई पदमबहादुरकै शव भनेर कसरी सनाखत गर्‍यो?

प्रहरीका अनुसार घटना सुनसरीको बराहक्षेत्र नगरपालिका–४ स्थित चतरा–पकली सडकखण्डमा भएको थियो। २०८३ जेठ २६ गते बिहान करिब साढे ८ बजे मोटरसाइकलको ठक्करबाट एक पैदलयात्री गम्भीर घाइते भएका थिए।

उपचारका लागि उनलाई बुढीगंगास्थित विराट टिचिङ अस्पताल लगिएको थियो। उपचारकै क्रममा मृत्यु भएपछि शव कोशी अस्पतालको शवगृहमा राखिएको थियो। मृतकको पहिचान खुल्न नसकेपछि प्रहरीले आफन्तलाई सम्पर्कमा आउन सार्वजनिक सूचना जारी गरेको थियो।

प्रहरीको सूचनापछि पदमबहादुरकी आमा अस्पताल पुगेकी थिइन्। उनले शव आफ्नै छोराको भएको बताएपछि प्रहरीले आवश्यक प्रक्रिया पूरा गरी शव परिवारलाई बुझाएको थियो। परिवारले त्यसपछि अन्त्येष्टि गरेको थियो।

लामो समय घरबाहिर थिए पदमबहादुर
इलाका प्रहरी कार्यालय लेटाङका अनुसार पदमबहादुर २०८२ माघदेखि घरबाहिर थिए। उनी घर छाडेर हिँड्ने गरेको जानकारी प्रहरीले परिवारबाट पाएको छ।

विवाहपछि श्रीमती अलग्गिएसँगै पदमबहादुर घरमा नियमित रूपमा नबस्ने गरेको बताइएको छ। लामो समय घरबाहिर रहेकाले परिवारलाई उनको अवस्थाबारे जानकारी थिएन।

यही परिस्थितिमा दुर्घटनामा मृत्यु भएका अज्ञात व्यक्तिको शव देखेपछि आमाले आफ्नै छोराको ठानेर सनाखत गरेको हुन सक्ने प्रहरीको प्रारम्भिक बुझाइ छ। तर, त्यसबेला शवको पहिचान कसरी गलत भयो भन्ने विषयमा अनुसन्धानबाट थप तथ्य खुल्न बाँकी छ।

बिहीबार काठमाडौंमा आयोजित नेशनल क्लाइमेट समिट–२०२६ मा बोल्दै मन्त्री खनालले जलवायु परिवर्तनका कारण हिमाली पारिस्थितिक प्रणालीमा परेको असर नेपालका लागि मात्र नभई विश्वकै साझा चुनौती बनेको बताए। हिमालको संरक्षण पानी, खाद्य सुरक्षा, ऊर्जा र अर्थतन्त्रसँग प्रत्यक्ष जोडिएकाले यसको सुरक्षा राष्ट्रिय हितसँगै अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय जिम्मेवारी पनि भएको उनको भनाइ छ।

बाढीपहिरोबाट ठूलो क्षति, पुनर्निर्माणमा अर्बौँ डलर आवश्यक

मन्त्री खनालका अनुसार गत अगस्ट २६ मा भोटेकोशी करिडोरमा आएको विनाशकारी बाढीपछि करिब छ साताको अवधिमा नेपालका तीन नदी करिडोरमा ठूला बाढीपहिरोका घटना भएका थिए। ती विपद्ले जनधन, पूर्वाधार, जीविकोपार्जन र अर्थतन्त्रमा गम्भीर क्षति पुर्‍याएका थिए।

अगस्टमा भएको विपद्बाट क्षतिग्रस्त संरचनाको पुनर्निर्माण तथा प्रभावित क्षेत्रको पुनःस्थापनाका लागि प्रारम्भिक आकलनअनुसार करिब ४ अर्ब ७० करोड अमेरिकी डलर आवश्यक पर्ने देखिएको उनले बताए। यो रकम नेपालको कुल गार्हस्थ्य उत्पादनको करिब १० प्रतिशत बराबर हुने उनको भनाइ छ।

कोप–३१ मा हिमाली मुद्दालाई प्राथमिकता

मन्त्री खनालले कोप–३१ मा नेपालले चार प्रमुख प्राथमिकताका साथ अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय जलवायु वार्तामा सहभागिता जनाउने बताए। पहिलो प्राथमिकता हिमाली क्षेत्रका मुद्दालाई विश्वव्यापी जलवायु वार्ताको केन्द्रमा राख्नु रहेको छ।

पेरिस सम्झौताले तय गरेको विश्वव्यापी तापक्रम वृद्धिलाई १.५ डिग्री सेल्सियसमा सीमित गर्ने लक्ष्य हिमाली मुलुकका लागि विशेष महत्त्वपूर्ण रहेको उनले उल्लेख गरे।

नेपालले सन् २०२४ मा आयोजना गरेको ‘इन्टरनेसनल एक्सपर्ट डाइलग अन माउन्टेन्स, पिपुल एन्ड क्लाइमेट चेन्ज’ तथा सन् २०२५ को सगरमाथा संवादबाट अघि बढाइएका पहललाई निरन्तरता दिने पनि उनले बताए। यसअन्तर्गत नियमित उच्चस्तरीय संवाद, छुट्टै हिमाल कार्ययोजना र विश्वव्यापी जलवायु संरचनामा हिमाली क्षेत्रका जोखिम समेट्न पैरवी गरिनेछ।

जलवायुजन्य हानि तथा नोक्सानीको मुद्दा उठाइने

नेपालको दोस्रो प्राथमिकता जलवायु परिवर्तनका कारण हुने हानि तथा नोक्सानीलाई सम्बोधन गर्नु रहेको मन्त्री खनालले बताए। जलवायु संकटबाट प्रभावित मुलुकलाई आवश्यक सहयोग उपलब्ध गराउनु अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय ऐक्यबद्धताको महत्त्वपूर्ण आधार हुनुपर्ने उनको भनाइ छ।

उनले हानि तथा नोक्सानी सम्बोधनसम्बन्धी कोषबाट नेपालका लागि २१ अर्ब ६० करोड अमेरिकी डलर विनियोजन गर्न प्रारम्भिक सहमति भएको र नेपाल यस्तो विनियोजन प्राप्त गर्ने पहिलो देश बनेको दाबी गरे।

यद्यपि, उक्त रकमको विवरण, सहमतिको प्रकृति र विनियोजनको आधिकारिक अवस्थाबारे थप पुष्टि आवश्यक छ। जलवायु परिवर्तनबाट प्रभावित देशले पर्याप्त स्रोतसाधन प्राप्त गर्नुपर्ने र उपलब्ध कोषमा सहज पहुँच हुनुपर्नेमा मन्त्री खनालले जोड दिए।

अनुकूलनका लागि २० अर्ब डलरसम्म आवश्यक

नेपालको तेस्रो प्राथमिकता जलवायु वित्तलाई सहज पहुँचयोग्य, न्यायोचित र राष्ट्रिय आवश्यकताप्रति उत्तरदायी बनाउनु रहेको छ।

मन्त्री खनालका अनुसार नेपालको तेस्रो राष्ट्रिय निर्धारित योगदान (एनडीसी ३.०) ले सन् २०२५ देखि २०३५ सम्म जलवायु अनुकूलनका लागि करिब १८ देखि २० अर्ब अमेरिकी डलर आवश्यक पर्ने देखाएको छ। जलवायु परिवर्तनको असर न्यूनीकरण गर्न तथा प्रभावित समुदायलाई अनुकूलनमा सहयोग पुर्‍याउन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय वित्तीय स्रोतको महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका रहने उनले बताए।

नेपालजस्ता जलवायु परिवर्तनको असरबाट बढी प्रभावित मुलुकले आफ्नो आवश्यकताअनुसार वित्तीय सहयोग प्राप्त गर्नुपर्नेमा उनले जोड दिए।

जलवायु न्याय र सीमान्तकृत समुदायको सहभागितामा जोड

नेपालको चौथो प्राथमिकता जलवायु न्यायलाई विश्वव्यापी प्रयासको केन्द्रमा राख्नु रहेको मन्त्री खनालले बताए।

विश्वव्यापी हरितगृह ग्यास उत्सर्जनमा नेपालको योगदान न्यून भए पनि जलवायु परिवर्तनका कारण देशले ठूलो क्षति व्यहोर्नुपरेको उनले उल्लेख गरे। वन, हिमनदी र हिमाली पारिस्थितिक प्रणालीको संरक्षणमार्फत नेपालले विश्वव्यापी पर्यावरणीय स्थिरतामा योगदान गरिरहेको उनको भनाइ छ।

उनले जलवायु परिवर्तनसम्बन्धी निर्णय प्रक्रियामा महिला, बालबालिका, आदिवासी जनजाति, अपाङ्गता भएका व्यक्ति तथा सीमान्तकृत समुदायको अर्थपूर्ण सहभागिता सुनिश्चित गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

हिमाली क्षेत्र र प्रशान्त महासागर एउटै जलवायु प्रणालीबाट जोडिएकाले ‘सगरमाथादेखि समुद्रसम्म’ को अवधारणा महत्त्वपूर्ण रहेको पनि उनले बताए।

मन्त्री खनालका अनुसार कोप–३१ मा नेपालले हिमाली क्षेत्रका जोखिमलाई अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय जलवायु एजेन्डामा स्थापित गर्ने, जलवायुजन्य क्षतिको सम्बोधनका लागि सहयोग जुटाउने, जलवायु वित्तमा सहज पहुँच सुनिश्चित गर्ने र जलवायु न्यायको मागलाई बलियो बनाउने प्रयास गर्नेछ।

हरिवंशदेखि आर्यनसम्म पाँच दाजुभाइको भावुक कथा! ‘पाँच पाण्डव’को नयाँ गीत सार्वजनिक, तिहारमा चलचित्र प्रदर्शन हुँदै!

तिहारको अवसर पारेर प्रदर्शनमा आउन लागेको नेपाली चलचित्र ‘पाँच पाण्डव’को नयाँ गीत ‘दाजु भाइजस्ता हुँदैनन् अरू’ सार्वजनिक भएको छ। दाजुभाइबीचको माया, विश्वास, एकता र पारिवारिक सम्बन्धलाई प्रस्तुत गरिएको गीत सार्वजनिक भएसँगै चलचित्रको चर्चा बढेको छ।

गीतमा चर्चित गायकद्वय सत्यराज आचार्य र स्वरूपराज आचार्यको स्वररहेको छ। अर्जुन पोखरेलको संगीत र डा. कृष्णहरि बरालको शब्द रहेको गीतले सुखदुःखमा दाजुभाइ एकअर्काको सहारा बन्नुपर्ने सन्देश दिन खोजेको छ।

गीतको भिडियोमा चलचित्रका मुख्य कलाकार हरिवंश आचार्य, जितु नेपाल, आर्यन सिग्देल, महेश त्रिपाठी र सुशील सिटौला देखिएका छन्। उनीहरूलाई पाँच पाण्डवको भूमिकामा प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ।

भिडियोमा दाजुभाइबीचको भावनात्मक सम्बन्धसँगै महाभारतको कथाबाट प्रेरित दृश्यहरू पनि समेटिएका छन्। समस्यामा परेका भाइहरूको खोजीमा स्वर्गलोकबाट युधिष्ठिर पृथ्वीमा आएको दृश्यले चलचित्रको कथावस्तुप्रति थप उत्सुकता जगाएको छ।

वसन्त निरौलाको निर्देशनमा बनेको चलचित्रमा दीपाश्री निरौला, सरिता गिरी, प्रशान्त ताम्राकार, इभा गिरीलगायतका कलाकारको समेत अभिनय रहेको छ। चलचित्रको कथा, पटकथा तथा संवाद सुशील पौडेलले लेखेका हुन्।

निर्माण पक्षका अनुसार ‘पाँच पाण्डव’ले महाभारतका पात्र र प्रतीकलाई आधुनिक नेपाली समाजसँग जोड्दै परिवार, सम्बन्ध र एकताको कथा प्रस्तुत गर्नेछ।

काली रानी फिल्म्सको ब्यानरमा निर्मित चलचित्र आगामी कात्तिक २० गते अर्थात् नोभेम्बर ६ देखि देशभरका सिनेमा हलमा प्रदर्शन हुने तयारीमा छ।

दाजुभाइको सम्बन्धमा आधारित भावुक गीत र चर्चित कलाकारहरूको उपस्थितिले ‘पाँच पाण्डव’प्रति दर्शकको चासो बढाएको छ। अब चलचित्रले प्रदर्शनपछि दर्शकबाट कस्तो प्रतिक्रिया पाउँछ भन्ने प्रतीक्षा छ।

नागढुंगा सुरुङमा शुल्क लागू हुँदै, कुन गाडीलाई कति?
काठमाडौं उपत्यका प्रवेश गर्ने तथा बाहिरिने सवारी चालकका लागि महत्त्वपूर्ण खबर छ। आउँदो कात्तिक १५ गते आइतबारदेखि नागढुंगा सुरुङमार्ग प्रयोग गर्ने सवारीसाधनले सडक उपभोग दस्तुर तिर्नुपर्ने भएको छ। नागढुंगा सुरुङमार्ग निर्माण आयोजनाले सार्वजनिक सूचना जारी गर्दै नयाँ शुल्कदर लागू हुने जानकारी दिएको हो।

सडक बोर्ड नेपालको निर्णयअनुसार सुरुङमार्ग प्रयोग गर्ने सवारीसाधनको प्रकार र काठमाडौं प्रवेश गर्ने वा बाहिरिने दिशाका आधारमा फरक–फरक शुल्क निर्धारण गरिएको छ। नयाँ व्यवस्था लागू भएपछि सुरुङमार्ग प्रयोग गर्ने चालकले तोकिएको दरअनुसार दस्तुर तिर्नुपर्नेछ।

कुन सवारीसाधनलाई कति शुल्क?
आयोजनाले सार्वजनिक गरेको शुल्कदरअनुसार कार, भ्यान, पिकअप, ट्याक्टर, माइक्रोबस तथा अन्य हलुका सवारीसाधनले काठमाडौं प्रवेश गर्दा ६५ रुपैयाँ र काठमाडौं उपत्यकाबाट बाहिरिँदा ६० रुपैयाँ तिर्नुपर्नेछ।

त्यस्तै, मिनी बस, मिनी टिपर तथा मिनी ट्रकले काठमाडौं प्रवेश गर्दा ११५ रुपैयाँ र बाहिरिँदा ८० रुपैयाँ शुल्क बुझाउनुपर्नेछ।

बस तथा ट्रकका लागि काठमाडौं प्रवेश गर्दा २६० रुपैयाँ र उपत्यकाबाट बाहिरिँदा २०० रुपैयाँ शुल्क तोकिएको छ। यसैगरी, मल्टी एक्सल ट्रक, अन्य ठूला सवारीसाधन तथा भारी उपकरणले काठमाडौं प्रवेश गर्दा ६०० रुपैयाँ र बाहिरिँदा २५० रुपैयाँ तिर्नुपर्नेछ।

सडक बोर्डको निर्णयअनुसार शुल्क
सडक बोर्ड नेपालको कार्यकारी समितिको २०८३ असोज १२ गतेको निर्णय तथा २०८२ चैत २६ गते नेपाल राजपत्रमा प्रकाशित सूचनाका आधारमा शुल्क संकलन गर्न लागिएको हो। नागढुंगा सुरुङमार्ग निर्माण आयोजनाले सुरुङ प्रयोग गर्ने सवारीधनी तथा चालकलाई तोकिएको दस्तुर तिरेर यात्रा गर्न अनुरोध गरेको छ। 

यससँगै कात्तिक १५ गतेदेखि नागढुंगा सुरुङमार्ग प्रयोग गर्ने सवारीसाधनले अनिवार्य रूपमा सडक उपभोग दस्तुर तिर्नुपर्नेछ। त्यसैले सुरुङमार्ग हुँदै काठमाडौं प्रवेश गर्ने वा बाहिरिने योजना बनाएका चालकले आफ्नो सवारीसाधनको वर्गअनुसार लाग्ने शुल्कबारे जानकारी लिनु आवश्यक छ।

अन्य जिल्लाबाट नेपाली नागरिकताको प्रमाणपत्र लिएका नागरिकले अब काठमाडौं उपत्यकाबाटै नागरिकताको प्रतिलिपि लिन पाउने भएका छन्। जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय काठमाडौंले नयाँ व्यवस्था सार्वजनिक गर्दै तोकिएका सर्त पूरा गर्ने नागरिकले काठमाडौं, ललितपुर र भक्तपुरका जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयबाट नागरिकताको प्रतिलिपि लिन सक्ने जनाएको छ।

सरकारको १०० बुँदे शासकीय सुधार कार्यसूचीको बुँदा नम्बर २१ तथा नेपाल नागरिकता (पाँचौँ संशोधन) नियमावली, २०८३ अनुसार यो व्यवस्था कार्यान्वयनमा ल्याइएको हो। यसले नागरिकताको प्रतिलिपि लिनकै लागि आफ्नो गृहजिल्ला पुग्नुपर्ने बाध्यता कम गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

नयाँ व्यवस्थाअनुसार बागमती, गण्डकी र लुम्बिनी प्रदेशबाट नागरिकता लिएका नागरिकले जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय काठमाडौं, कर्णाली र सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशबाट नागरिकता लिएकाले जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय ललितपुर तथा कोशी र मधेश प्रदेशबाट नागरिकता लिएकाले जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय भक्तपुर बाट प्रतिलिपिका लागि आवेदन दिन सक्नेछन्।

तर, नागरिकताको प्रतिलिपि लिनका लागि सम्बन्धित विवरण र अभिलेख मिलेको हुनुपर्नेछ। बागमती, गण्डकी र लुम्बिनी प्रदेशबाट नागरिकता लिएका व्यक्तिको हकमा राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्र व्यवस्थापन सूचना प्रणाली (NIDMIS) र नागरिकता सूचना व्यवस्थापन प्रणाली (CCIMS) मा रहेको जैविक विवरण मिल्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था छ।

यदि सम्बन्धित कार्यालयमा नागरिकताको अभिलेख फेला नपरेमा वा नाम, थर तथा जन्ममितिजस्ता विवरण सच्याउनुपर्ने भएमा भने नागरिकता जारी भएको सम्बन्धित जिल्लामै सम्पर्क गर्नुपर्नेछ। अभिलेख शंकास्पद देखिएमा पनि नागरिकता जारी गर्ने जिल्लाबाट आवश्यक विवरण पुष्टि गर्नुपर्ने हुन्छ।

यस व्यवस्थाले काठमाडौं उपत्यकामा बसोबास गर्दै आएका अन्य जिल्लाका नागरिकलाई नागरिकताको प्रतिलिपि लिन सहज बनाउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ। यद्यपि, प्रतिलिपि प्राप्त गर्न सम्बन्धित जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयले तोकेका प्रक्रिया र आवश्यक सर्तहरू पूरा गर्नुपर्नेछ।

A WWII DESTROYER WAS FOUND MORE THAN 6,400 METRES UNDER THE OCEAN!

For decades, the USS Johnston rested in the darkness of the Philippine Sea, more than 6 kilometres beneath the surface.

The American destroyer sank on October 25, 1944, during the Battle off Samar in World War II. Despite facing a vastly larger Japanese force, the ship fought to protect vulnerable American escort carriers.

In 2019, explorers located wreckage believed to be the Johnston. But the mystery was finally solved in March 2021, when a crewed deep-sea submersible reached the main wreck at approximately 6,456 metres (21,180 feet).

The biggest confirmation?

The ship’s hull number 557 was still visible after more than 76 years underwater.

Of the 327 crew members, 141 survived.

Imagine discovering a ship resting in complete darkness, with its identity still written on its bow after all those years.

What other forgotten secrets could be waiting in the deepest parts of our oceans?

Share your thoughts in the comments, and follow Lost & Unsolved History for more extraordinary real discoveries.

#USSJohnston #DeepSeaDiscovery #WWIIHistory #OceanMystery #LostAndUnsolvedHistory

TWO RELOCATED MARINE MAMMALS DIE AS NECROPSIES REVEAL SERIOUS HEALTH CONCERNS

Beluga whale Jelly Bean and bottlenose dolphin Echo died after arriving at their new facilities. Necropsies reportedly identified complications involving the heart, thyroid, adrenal glands, and nervous tissue.

Their deaths have raised further concerns about the health risks marine mammals may face during relocation and the importance of careful veterinary monitoring.

Understanding the findings may help experts assess the animals’ conditions and improve care for other relocated marine mammals.

Research reported by ScienceDaily has identified a distinct division among West Coast transient killer whales, with inner-coast and outer-coast groups using different hunting grounds and targeting different prey.

These orcas are specialized marine-mammal hunters, and their movements and feeding habits can vary depending on where they live and what food is available.

Understanding these population differences helps researchers learn how orcas adapt to their environments and why protecting diverse coastal habitats matters.

The remaining relocated whales at facilities such as SeaWorld San Antonio and Georgia Aquarium are reportedly stable and receiving around-the-clock veterinary monitoring.

Following concerns over the health and deaths of some animals involved in recent relocations, their condition remains an important focus for animal-care teams.

Continued monitoring and transparent updates will be essential to understanding how the whales are adjusting to their new environments.

US Army Fans AI.caption:
When missing by an inch means total mission failure, you build a firing solution out of whatever terrain the mountain gives you.

A Delta Force precision marksman locked behind his rifle system during high-angle mountain sniper training in Hat Creek, Idaho.

This image is a masterclass in modern, non-traditional long-range shooting. In the rugged backcountry, flat shooting benches and prone mats do not exist. Instead, the shooter uses a gnarled tree crook as an improvised front rest, cushioning the chassis on a shooting bag while anchoring his stance on high-elevation carbon-fiber tripod legs.

Look at the hardware mounted to the rifle platform. He is running an advanced precision bolt-action rifle chambered for long-range interdiction, fitted with a high-magnification optic, top-mounted micro red dot for fast target transitions, a dedicated sound suppressor, and electro-optical targeting gear riding the 12 o'clock rail. Behind him sits a secondary heavy tripod rig running an electro-optical spotter setup to call wind and trace across jagged canyon lines.

Operating out of places like the remote Hat Creek training facilities allows Tier 1 snipers to hone cold-bore precision at extreme angles, factoring in brutal mountain updrafts, thin air, and mirage over distances exceeding 1,000 yards.

Low-key civilian outerwear, ball cap, and pure surgical discipline.

Delta Force sniper section. The Unit.

“DON’T WASTE YOUR TIME ON ME. I AM IN THE EXPECTANT CATEGORY. I’M DONE HERE.” — Green Beret Warrant Officer Nick Lavery on The Shawn Ryan Show.

In one of the most unforgettable moments on The Shawn Ryan Show, Special Forces Warrant Officer Nick "The Machine" Lavery recounted the insider attack in Afghanistan where he threw himself in front of a rookie soldier to absorb point-blank machine gun fire.

In his own words:

“I snap my head around and see what’s happening. A gunner 15 feet away from the group ripping into the crowd with a PKM. Guys are dropping. Chaos.

My training tells me: move to cover, eliminate the threat. But six feet in front of me is one of our infantry uplift soldiers—young kid, first deployment, fresh out of basic. He’s 15 feet in front of a guy shooting a machine gun in his general direction, frozen like a deer in the headlights.

Seeing that prompted me to move towards him rather than to cover. I put myself in between him and the shooter, back to the gun. I hit him with such velocity that when we made contact, I took a round to the back of my leg.

I fall chest to chest on top of him. A PKM from 15 feet feels like a sledgehammer smashing into your body. Then boom, boom, boom a couple more impacts.

I check the kid. He’s in shock, pale, but no holes in his body. He’s breathing.

So now let’s see what’s going on with me. I rip open what’s left of my pant leg. My right leg is just f**king mangled—hanging meat, tissue, and exposed bone. I am hissing blood out of my thigh. There is a river flowing from where I was struck. My femoral artery is severed. I have maybe eight or nine minutes before I bleed out completely.

One of my teammates gets over to me. The look on his face said everything: Nick’s not going to make it.

I looked at him and said, ‘Listen man, go work on someone you can save. I am in the expectant category here in triage. Don’t waste your time, precious seconds, and resources on me, because I’m done here.’”

His teammates refused to quit on him. They cranked tourniquets onto his mangled leg, stabilized him under fire, and got him on a medevac bird.

Not only did Nick survive having his leg amputated above the knee, but he also refused medical retirement. He underwent grueling rehab, relearned how to shoot, sprint, and clear rooms on a carbon-fiber prosthetic, and became the first active-duty Green Beret in history to return to combat as an above-the-knee amputee.

Ordering your brothers to leave you behind to save others while you bleed out from a severed femoral artery is the ultimate definition of selfless service.

Drop a salute in the comments for Nick "The Machine" Lavery.

REST IN PEACE: The U.S. Army has identified the soldier tragically killed during a training exercise at Fort Lee as 23-year-old Private Nicholas Chavira.

Army officials confirmed that Private Chavira lost his life during an on-post military training exercise in Prince George County, Virginia, according to reporting from WTVR CBS 6 and Hoodline.

What officials have confirmed:

Private Chavira died during active military training operations in a designated training area on post.

 Military officials stated that no foul play is suspected, and the Army has launched an official investigation into the exact circumstances surrounding the fatal incident.

 Every day, young men and women step forward and put their lives on the line in demanding, high-risk training environments across the country to prepare for combat operations downrange.

Losing a young soldier at 23 years old in the line of duty is an absolute heartbreak.

Please take a moment to keep Private Nicholas Chavira’s family, loved ones, and unit in your thoughts and prayers.
Rest Easy

Ukraine reports Russian military personnel losses reached an estimated 49,040 in October—the highest single-month casualty toll of the entire war.

According to official reporting from the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, Russian combat personnel losses (killed and severely wounded) in October 2026 surpassed the previous all-time monthly high of 48,670 set in December 2024.

The operational reality behind the numbers:

 That figure represents an average of roughly 1,690 Russian soldiers lost every 24 hours throughout October across intense frontline sectors including Pokrovsk, Kurakhove, Toretsk, and the Kursk salient.

Combat hexacopters and FPV strike teams played a decisive role in driving these numbers. Data tracked by Ukrainian forces indicates drone operations alone accounted for over 27,800 Russian personnel casualties in the first 25 days of the month.

Moscow continues relying on persistent dismounted infantry assaults and mechanized pushes to seize territory across eastern Ukraine before winter freezes the ground and shifts battlefield conditions.

Despite staggering monthly casualties, Russian forces continue pressing forward meter by meter in the Donbas.

At a burn rate of nearly 50,000 personnel per month, how long can Russian offensive momentum realistically hold out before manpower shortages force an operational pause?

“I FKING LOST THE WILL TO LIVE. SO I DID WHAT I DID.” — Cain Velasquez breaks his silence on The Shawn Ryan Show.

In an emotional sit-down interview on The Shawn Ryan Show, former two-time UFC Heavyweight Champion Cain Velasquez opened up about the February 2022 high-speed chase and shooting that completely altered the trajectory of his life.

In his own words:

“My son was in bed and told me things that are happening to him at daycare. So I ask questions about what happened, he tells me, I said ‘how long has this been going on?’  he said ‘a while.’

So I did what we’re supposed to do. Make a report and call the authorities. They book him, he gets out on Friday that same week with no ankle monitor, nothing. He’s out in two days.

Just seeing my son, the trauma coming out, seeing the hurt in him, him breaking down crying. Seeing Michelle [his wife] break down, and not being able to do anything about it.

Now looking at the signs, my son started digressing in his potty training. So he would just wet himself. He was avoiding going to the bathroom.

I lost it. I f**king lost the will to live. Didn’t care about dying or anything. I was in a different place at that moment. So I did what I did.

I went on an 11-mile chase shooting at him.”

After years of legal battles, months spent in solitary confinement, and a prison sentence, Velasquez was released earlier this year to reunite with his family and return to coaching.

When the justice system releases an alleged child abuser back onto the streets in 48 hours with no monitor, what goes through a father's mind?

Did Cain do what any protective father pushed past the brink would do? Drop your take below.

Imagine being strapped into a seat facing backward, in the windowless belly of a propeller plane on the deck of an aircraft carrier in the middle of the ocean. A catapult grabs the plane, and in about two seconds you go from a dead stop to roughly 130 miles an hour and off the bow, slammed back into your seat the whole way.

For 60 years, this was the normal way to reach a US Navy carrier at sea, and the plane that did it was the C-2 Greyhound. The landing was just as wild: the Greyhound caught a steel cable with a hook on its tail, going from flying speed to a dead stop in under 400 feet. First-timers never forgot it.

But it was far more than a thrill ride. Its job was Carrier Onboard Delivery, flying the parts, people, and mail a carrier needs out to the ship while it is underway, sometimes hundreds of miles from land. And of everything it carried, nothing meant more to the crews than the mail: the letters and packages from home that a sailor on a long deployment waits weeks to hold. A single pair of Greyhounds could move a million pounds of cargo and 5,000 passengers in one deployment. Quietly, it kept the world's most powerful warships running.

After six decades, the Greyhound flew its last flight earlier in 2026, retired to a museum in Pensacola and replaced by the CMV-22B Osprey. "It's very sad to me," said the pilot of that final flight, "but I feel a lot of satisfaction that we did it safely."

The three-star general fired as the military's top strategist has admitted to leaking classified intelligence on Iran and Ukraine.

In one of the most explosive national security breaches inside the building in decades, Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia the former Director for Strategy, Plans, and Policy on the Joint Staff (J5) admitted to leaking classified military intelligence to the media, according to reporting from Axios and The Washington Post.

The breakdown of the ouster:

As the Joint Staff J5, Sylvia was the U.S. military's lead strategic war planner, responsible for shaping global contingency operations, force posture, and direct combat advice for the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs and the Secretary of Defense.

Sylvia was abruptly relieved of his duties by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after allegedly failing three consecutive counterintelligence polygraph examinations during an aggressive Pentagon internal leak probe.

 Pentagon officials confirmed that Sylvia subsequently admitted to unauthorized disclosures of classified information regarding sensitive U.S. contingency planning for war with Iran and ongoing military operations in Ukraine.

While junior enlisted service members and NCOs routinely face immediate pretrial confinement, Leavenworth prison sentences, and dishonorable discharges under the UCMJ for mishandling classified documents, senior flag officers have historically been allowed to quietly retire.

A three-star general sitting on the Joint Staff leaking classified war plans to reporters strikes at the very core of military chain of command and national security.

The lone Navy corpsman who sprinted into a burning building to save six coalition soldiers.

On the night of March 12 in northern Iraq, an enemy one-way attack drone detonated roughly 25 meters from the living quarters of Navy Hospital Corpsman 2nd Class (HM2) Jajuan Hernandez.

Serving as the sole U.S. medic at the outpost while attached to the 2nd Marine Raider Battalion (MARSOC), Hernandez grabbed his weapon, body armor, and trauma bag, sprinting directly toward the fire amidst secondary ammunition explosions.

He arrived at a demolished berthing area to find seven critically wounded French coalition soldiers lying in the dark.

Despite severe language barriers, Hernandez directed nearby Marine Raiders to assist with bandaging and hypothermia blankets while personally executing advanced, life-saving battlefield surgical procedures:

Blunt finger thoracostomy and needle decompression (making incisions to vent air pressure around collapsed lungs and the heart).

Administering fresh whole blood intraosseously ("via the bone").

Applying tourniquets and chest seals under active secondary cook-offs.

 Acting Surgeon General of the Navy Rear Adm. Matthew Case credited Hernandez's quick thinking with directly saving the lives of six French soldiers until medical evacuations could arrive.

In late September, Hernandez was officially presented with the Armed Services YMCA's prestigious 2026 Angels of the Battlefield Award in Washington, D.C.

There is no bond on the battlefield quite like the one between Marines and their Doc.

BREAKING IN EUROPE: Chaos erupts in Warsaw as police deploy outside Poland’s top constitutional court amid accusations of an unconstitutional coup.

A major constitutional showdown has paralyzed Poland’s capital tonight. Polish police vans cordoned off the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw after government-backed judges moved to suspend the court's president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and vice president, triggering claims of an executive power grab.

The escalation forced Polish President Karol Nawrocki to abruptly abort an official diplomatic flight to Senegal mid-air over southern Spain and race back to Warsaw, writing: "In such a moment the president must be in Poland. I am interrupting the flight to Senegal. I am returning."

What is unfolding on the ground:

Tactical police units surrounded the perimeter of the tribunal building on Wiejska Street as crowds gathered and scuffles broke out. Police confirmed multiple detentions after protesters attempted to scale the security fence.

 Opposition leader Jarosław Kaczyński arrived outside the court, denouncing the move as an "illegal coup against the Constitutional Tribunal" orchestrated by Prime Minister Donald Tusk's pro-EU coalition.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk forcefully defended the measures on X, stating: "Restoring the rule of law is our duty. After years of PiS lawlessness, it is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and requires decisive action. There is no other way."

Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek announced criminal applications to strip the tribunal leadership of their judicial immunity, while the ousted court leadership rejected the orders as completely void and unconstitutional.

With the president rushing back to the capital and police holding the perimeter, Poland is facing its deepest constitutional crisis in modern history.

Palm Beach, Florida.

In an unprecedented escalation of executive protection, the U.S. military and Secret Service have deployed mobile surface-to-air missile systems directly outside Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate.

Moored on a floating industrial barge in the Intracoastal Waterway right off the property's perimeter, photos confirm a pair of AN/TWQ-1 Avenger Air Defense Systems:

The Hardware: High-mobility Humvees outfitted with twin missile pods carrying eight ready-to-fire FIM-92 Stinger missiles, backed by a high-rate-of-fire .50-caliber M3P machine gun.

Target Profile: The Avenger platform is engineered specifically for short-range air defense (SHORAD), designed to intercept low-altitude, high-speed threats including low-flying aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering suicide drones.

Layered Defense: The floating missile battery operates alongside expanded air defense radar coverage tied into NORAD, establishing a hardened dome over the estate and nearby flight corridors.

While surface-to-air missile rings (like NASAMS and Avenger batteries) have quietly guarded the White House and the National Capital Region since 9/11, stationing military anti-aircraft missile platforms on domestic waterways outside a private residence in Florida marks an extraordinary chapter in modern security.

Federal authorities enacted the heightened measures following elevated threat assessments, foreign assassination threats from Iran, and the rising global reality of cheap, asymmetric drone warfare.

The nature of executive protection has changed forever.

Is deploying military anti-aircraft missile systems on domestic waterways a necessary response to modern drone threats, or a sign of how volatile security has become?

How much has the war with Iran cost the United States? It is a simple question with a surprisingly slippery answer.

The most recent official estimate, from US Central Command, puts the figure at just over 47 billion dollars. The largest cost by far is munitions, nearly 30 billion dollars' worth expended since the fighting began in February 2026, plus about 7.6 billion for air operations and 1.5 billion for the Navy-led blockade of Iran.

But even that number leaves things out. It does not include the cost of repairing the widespread damage done to US bases hit by Iranian attacks, which the Pentagon says it cannot fully estimate yet. That is a big reason the estimates vary so much: an earlier public figure put the cost around 25 billion, while US officials told CBS and CNN the real total was already closer to 40 to 50 billion, and some projections run higher still once long-term costs like replacing munitions are counted.

None of the numbers is exactly wrong. They are measuring different things over different timeframes. The honest answer to what the Iran war has cost is a range, not a single figure: at least 47 billion by the military's own count, and quite possibly more once the full picture comes in.

A U.S. Army sniper team with the Jalalabad Provincial Reconstruction Team scans the horizon in Nangarhar Province, Afghanistan, on October 19, 2006. Provincial Reconstruction Teams brought together soldiers, civilian experts, and government officials to support reconstruction projects and local governance, but they still had to operate in a combat zone where threats could appear at any moment.

That's where teams like this came in. While engineers met with local leaders, inspected projects, and worked with communities, snipers provided overwatch, watching the high ground, routes, and approaches for anything out of place. Their job was to see danger before it reached the people they were protecting.

It's patient, demanding work that rarely gets noticed, and when it's done right, nothing happens at all.

Behind closed doors, the Pentagon has delivered a blunt message to European NATO allies: tone down the aggressive public rhetoric on Russia.

According to defense officials and diplomatic sources, U.S. defense leadership has privately urged several European allies—particularly frontline Baltic nations like Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia—to "cool" their public warnings regarding the threat of direct military conflict with Moscow.

The Pentagon’s core concern: uncontrolled escalation.

Avoiding the Cornered Rat Scenario: Washington warned that hyper-aggressive rhetoric from European leaders—declaring that direct war with Russia is inevitable or framing conflict in absolute terms—risks backing the Kremlin into an escalatory corner and removing diplomatic off-ramps.

Strategic Discipline: U.S. defense strategists are pushing for calibrated messaging, arguing that reckless rhetoric from allies who rely on American military backing can trigger accidental miscalculations that spiral into an Article 5 clash.

The quiet pushback exposes a growing rift inside the alliance:

Frontline European Allies argue that sounding the alarm and showing relentless public defiance is the only deterrent Moscow respects, warning that softening rhetoric projects weakness.

Washington Strategists argue that loose talk and public posturing complicate deterrence and increase the danger of sleepwalking into a catastrophic third world war.

When the stakes involve nuclear-armed superpowers, every word matters.

Is the Pentagon right to demand disciplined rhetoric to avoid war, or should European allies speak out forcefully against Russian aggression?

The War Department is officially launching the Chaplain In-Service Procurement Program.

In a major shift for military personnel pipelines, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announced that the Pentagon is establishing the Chaplain In-Service Procurement Program (CH-ISPP)—creating a dedicated pathway for active-duty enlisted troops to commission as military chaplains.

The announcement follows Hegseth's creation of the Office of Religious Affairs aimed at prioritizing spiritual readiness and troop resilience across the force.

Key details of the new program:

 Geared toward active-duty enlisted service members (with a minimum rank of E-5) who have a calling to military ministry.

 The program provides qualified NCOs with an active-duty commissioning route to complete their Master of Divinity (MDiv), secure ecclesiastical endorsement from their respective faith tradition, and pin on chaplain insignia without sacrificing military family financial stability.

 Proponents emphasize that bringing experienced NCOs who already understand deployment stress, unit culture, and combat hardship into the chaplaincy will bridge the trust gap between junior enlisted troops and staff officers, reinforcing mental health and suicide prevention efforts.

Transitioning seasoned enlisted leaders directly into the chaplain corps brings a unique frontline perspective to military ministry.

Do you think drawing chaplains directly from the enlisted NCO ranks will strengthen unit morale, or should the military keep relying primarily on civilian seminary recruitment?

Millions of UFC fans recognize his face and iconic braided mustache inside the Octagon.

But long before he ever stepped into a cage, Mike Beltran was holding the line on the frontlines of American law enforcement.

After serving his country in the United States Marine Corps, Beltran joined the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD)—kicking off a legendary 32-year career:

The County Jails: Cutting his teeth in the toughest detention facilities in California.

Gang Suppression: Working street-level enforcement against violent criminal syndicates across East LA.

Deep Undercover: Infiltrating high-level narcotics trafficking rings where one misstep meant sudden death.

DEA Task Force Officer: Spending his final six years working federal drug enforcement operations taking down international cartels.

From gun battles and cartel stings to sharing the cage with heavyweight champions, Beltran brought the exact same ethos to officiating that he lived in uniform: calm authority, split-second decisiveness, and an uncompromising commitment to protecting human life.

After nearly 32 years of protecting the citizens of Los Angeles County, Detective Mike Beltran has officially hung up his duty belt.

Pictured on the left is a young Mike Vining during his time as an Explosive Ordnance Disposal specialist in the Vietnam War. The photo was taken just before Christmas 1970 at Tay Ninh, during the cleanup of an ammunition bunker filled with MK 45 aircraft flares, 20mm rounds, and 40mm M406 grenades. Vining ended the job covered in fiberglass from the burned out flares, while South Vietnamese Army soldiers worked nearby trying to pull the parachutes out of them.

It was dirty, dangerous work, the kind EOD techs did every day without much recognition. That same tour also saw his team destroy the largest enemy ammunition cache found during the war.

The photo on the right shows Vining at his retirement, after 31 years of service. Delta Force A Squadron operator Lee Vampola, pictured on the far left, unfurls the American flag with his assault troop on a windswept ridgeline.   Born in 1985 and taken far too soon in 2024, Vampola belonged to the rarest breed of combat warriors. To earn a spot inside 1st Special Forces Operational Detachment-Delta demands surviving one of the most punishing, mentally exhausting selection courses known to the modern military. Men like Lee chose that fire willingly.   Look at the team dynamic captured in this mountain setting. This rare look shows an Uruguayan military member holding an iconic, combat-proven M1A1 Thompson submachine gun—a weapon that first saw action on the battlefields of World War II over 80 years ago.   

Originally acquired through mid-20th-century U.S. military aid programs, the heavy, milled-steel M1A1 Thompson served as a frontline submachine gun in Uruguay until the mid-1980s, when it was officially replaced by the 9mm Argentine-made FMK-3 submachine gun. 

Rather than melting down or destroying obsolete small arms when new rifles arrive, the Uruguayan military has historically maintained a policy of preserving older weapons in deep-storage armories. Because of this, classic firearms like the M1A1 Thompson, M1 Garand, and M1 Carbine occasionally resurface for specialized familiarity training, reserve exercises, or ceremonial duties. 

Weighing in at roughly 10 pounds unloaded and firing the hard-hitting .45 ACP cartridge at 700+ rounds per minute, the simplified wartime M1A1 design is practically indestructible—proving that good steel and timeless engineering never truly go out of style.

On April 7, 2003, during the fierce opening days of Operation Iraqi Freedom, U.S. Air Force Captain (later Colonel) Kim "Killer Chick" Campbell cemented her place in aviation legend when her A-10 Thunderbolt II took a direct hit over downtown Baghdad—and she refused to bail out.   

While diving below cloud cover to deliver close-air support for pinned-down U.S. ground troops near the Tigris River, Campbell had just finished firing her 30mm GAU-8 Avenger cannon and rockets when a surface-to-air missile slammed into the rear of her Warthog. The blast shredded her horizontal stabilizer, punched over 150 shrapnel holes into the fuselage and right engine cowling, and instantly severed both redundant hydraulic systems. 

As the crippled jet rolled violently left and pitched straight toward the streets of central Baghdad, Campbell knew ejecting meant parachuting directly into enemy hands. In a split second, she flipped the switch to manual reversion—a mechanical backup system of pulleys, cranks, and steel cables that pilots compare to steering a heavy truck with the stick stuck in quick-setting cement. 

Escorted by her flight lead, Lt. Col. Richard "Bino" Turner, Campbell muscled the battered Warthog for an hour over 300 miles back to Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. Rather than ejecting over friendly territory as the flight manual suggests, she elected to land the aircraft with no hydraulic flight controls, no speed brakes, and no normal steering—setting it down so smoothly that the wing's chief of safety remarked she landed it better with no hydraulics than most pilots do with all systems operational. She was awarded the Distinguished Flying Cross for her extraordinary airmanship under fire.

A U.S. Marine with 1st Battalion, 8th Marines, fires a Mk 153 Mod 0 SMAW in Fallujah, Iraq, in November 2004. A comprehensive U.S. Army medical study examining the brutal physical toll of Ranger School has revealed that female soldiers who complete the course finish in better overall physiological condition than their male counterparts, experiencing significantly less hormonal disruption and preserving a higher percentage of lean muscle mass. 

Conducted by researchers from the U.S. Army Research Institute of Environmental Medicine (USARIEM) and published in the Journal of Applied Physiology and Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise, the study tracked male and female candidates through the 61+ days of severe caloric deprivation, minimal sleep, and non-stop physical exertion across the Darby, Mountain, and Swamp phases. 

While male soldiers entered and exited the course with higher absolute strength and power, their bodies experienced a far steeper physiological crash. Men lost significantly more total body mass and lean muscle tissue, whereas female candidates metabolized fat stores more efficiently—preserving their fat-free muscle mass to a much greater extent and exhibiting fewer extreme drops in metabolic and endocrine hormone markers. 

Lead researcher James McClung noted that while both sexes suffered identical declines in sleep quality and physical output metrics over the two-month course, female physiology proved remarkably resilient against prolonged starvation and multi-stressor exhaustion, concluding: "An elite warfighter is an elite warfighter. It doesn't matter what your sex is."

A Salvadoran soldier carries one of the more unusual rifle setups you'll ever see: an M16 fitted with an M203 grenade launcher and an M72 LAW rocket launcher mounted on top. That's a rifle, a 40mm grenade launcher, and a 66mm anti-armor rocket all in one package.

During El Salvador's civil war in the 1980s, the Salvadoran Army received large amounts of American equipment, including M16s, M203s, and M72 LAWs, which made a combination like this possible. In close fights against guerrilla forces in mountains, villages, and dense vegetation, having that much firepower within reach could make all the difference, even if mounting it all together wasn't exactly standard practice.

Whether this was a field modification or a one off experiment, it was definitely not light, and probably not great for balance.

Can a dedicated 26-Marine Scout Platoon fully replace the legendary Scout Sniper platoons and give infantry commanders the ultimate eyes and ears on the modern battlefield? 

The U.S. Marine Corps’ newest primary infantry career field—the 0315 Marine Scout—is officially in effect, establishing a dedicated reconnaissance and surveillance pipeline on the heels of the Corps' controversial decision to phase out traditional Scout Sniper platoons in 2023.   

Previously treated as an additional skillset rather than a standalone career path, Marine Scouts now hold their own Primary Military Occupational Specialty (PMOS 0315) alongside riflemen (0311), machine gunners (0331), and mortarmen (0341). 

These specially trained Marines populate a 26-Marine Scout Platoon inside each infantry battalion—as well as scout teams within Light Armored Reconnaissance (LAR) battalions. Each scout team also embeds a certified Joint Fires Observer (JFO) capable of calling in devastating air and artillery strikes on high-value enemy targets. 

Trained in advanced fieldcraft, stealth, unmanned aerial systems, and assured long-range communications, 0315 Scouts are built to slip ahead of the main force, map routes to the objective, and extend an infantry battalion's sensing capabilities across contested littoral and inland environments.

Should mandatory "religious liberty training" and expanded roles for chaplains be implemented across the entire U.S. military?   

U.S. service members and commanders could soon be required to complete annual "religious liberty training" following sweeping recommendations from a White House-directed commission aimed at expanding faith-based protections across the armed forces.   

Chaired by Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick and former cabinet secretary Ben Carson, the federal Religious Liberty Commission issued a comprehensive report urging the Pentagon to implement annual training on religious accommodations, protect personal religious expression in the ranks, and integrate "religious liberty impact assessments" into operational planning.

Cody Alford lived at the sharp end of the spear. He deployed on multiple combat tours to Iraq and Afghanistan, leading sniper teams, kicking doors, and surviving under relentless enemy fire.

He earned the Bronze Star with Valor. But the battlefield takes a toll that body armor can't stop.

Hundreds of close-range breaching blasts, artillery concussions, and IED shockwaves tore through his brain. By the end of his career, Cody was suffering from severe Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), neurological breakdown, vestibular failure, and crippling PTSD.

His body and mind were shutting down.

When the uniform came off, the silence was louder than gunfire. Cody found himself stripped of his identity, struggling through neurological fog, and fighting just to function each day.

But instead of surrendering to the spiral, Cody chose to wage a new war—the war for his own mind and life.

Through intense neuro-rehabilitation, discipline, and honest self-examination, he rebuilt himself from the inside out.

He shared his entire journey on The Shawn Ryan Show, giving millions of veterans permission to acknowledge their invisible combat injuries and seek real healing. Today, through his platform We Are The They, he mentors people to break through mental barriers and conquer their internal battles.

The scars you can't see are often the hardest to heal.

True strength isn’t staying unbroken. True strength is picking up the pieces and forging yourself into something stronger.

On the night of November 13, 2015, during the final assault on the Bataclan, operators from the BRI, the Paris police's Brigade de Recherche et d'Intervention, advanced down a narrow corridor where two Islamist terrorists were holding eleven hostages. With nowhere to maneuver and the terrorists firing straight down the corridor at them, the operators moved forward behind the Ramsès, a heavy ballistic shield that reportedly absorbed more than 27 bullet impacts during the assault.

Every step forward was taken under fire, with the officers fully aware of what was waiting at the end of that corridor. The terrorists were armed and wearing explosive vests, and the hostages were trapped between them and the police. The BRI pushed through anyway, ended the threat, and brought the hostages out alive.

That night, 130 people were killed in coordinated attacks across Paris, 90 of them inside the Bataclan. In the middle of that horror, a small team of police officers walked toward the gunfire behind a shield because someone had to.

For the first time since the Korean War, the U.S. Army is actively preparing for the grimmest reality of large-scale combat: digging temporary mass graves directly on the battlefield.

During recent high-intensity readiness exercises at Fort Liberty, North Carolina, combat engineers from the 20th Engineer Brigade, soldiers from the 3rd Corps Sustainment Command, mortuary affairs specialists, and Army chaplains trained with heavy bulldozers and excavators to establish standardized field burial sites.

The metrics from the exercise are chilling:

Standardized burial trenches for 20 fallen soldiers can be excavated in just 75 minutes.

Using eight bulldozers and four military excavators, an engineering unit could temporarily inter the remains of up to 2,400 soldiers within a single 24-hour window.

For the past 20 years in Iraq and Afghanistan, the U.S. military enjoyed complete air dominance. Every fallen warrior was treated with reverent custody and flown directly home to Dover Air Force Base within days.

But Pentagon war games for a potential clash against a near-peer adversary—such as China or Russia—reveal a brutal reality:

Contested airspace, anti-ship missiles, and cyber-disrupted logistics could sever supply lines for weeks.

Immediate air repatriation would be physically impossible, and casualty counts could reach thousands in days.

Frontline units would be forced to temporarily inter fallen soldiers in the dirt to maintain positive identification, prevent disease, and protect remains until the combat zone can be secured for repatriation.

As Sergeant 1st Class Delbert Ruede stated during the drills: "If we went to war tomorrow, we would be making this up as we went along. What we are doing here is taking a scientific, field-tested approach so that we can maintain positive control and respectfully care for our fallen."

Practicing the unthinkable is the starkest sign yet of how seriously military planners view the threat of major war.

Is the military being responsibly realistic about near-peer warfare, or is this a chilling warning of where global tensions are heading?

Soldiers from the Rhodesian Light Infantry practice with their FN FAL rifles on a firing range, around 1977. Known as "The Saints," the RLI was a light infantry commando battalion that built its reputation during the Rhodesian Bush War, and is still often discussed among the most effective counterinsurgency units of its era.

Its fame came from Fireforce, a rapid reaction tactic in which small groups of soldiers were flown into contact by helicopter, often supported by paratroopers dropped from Dakotas, to surround and engage insurgent groups within minutes of them being spotted. At the height of the war, RLI troopers could find themselves deployed into action several times in a short period, and many made combat parachute jumps far more often than soldiers in most modern armies.

The FN FAL was their standard rifle, a reliable 7.62mm battle rifle well suited to the open bush and the close, fast engagements that Fireforce produced.

The Pentagon, U.S. Army Criminal Investigation Division (CID), and U.S. Cyber Command are officially investigating a wave of simultaneous, catastrophic freezer meltdowns across military base commissaries as a suspected foreign cyberattack.

In recent weeks, commercial refrigeration systems at commissaries across multiple major military installations including Fort Huachuca and bases across several states inexplicably malfunctioned at the exact same time. The sudden temperature overrides thawed massive freezer rows, spoiling hundreds of thousands of dollars in groceries and leaving military families with empty shelves.

Federal investigators quickly connected the dots: the incident closely mirrors a sophisticated cyberattack in France that remotely hacked and shut down environmental cooling controls across more than 350 commercial supermarkets.

While spoiled commissary food might sound like an annoyance on the surface, cybersecurity and military intelligence analysts warn that this is a classic asymmetric infrastructure probe:

Operational Technology (OT) Infiltration: Hostile nation-state hacking groups (such as China or Russia) are actively testing their ability to breach the industrial control systems and software running U.S. military installations.

The Wartime Threat: If foreign hackers can remotely shut down cooling systems in base grocery stores, the exact same networked SCADA vulnerabilities can be used during a conflict to overheat classified supercomputer data centers, ruin temperature-sensitive missile propellant in munitions depots, and destroy military medical blood and vaccine banks.

Gray-zone cyber warfare isn't coming in the future—it's already hitting domestic bases inside our own borders.

Is targeting grocery stores and base infrastructure an early warning of a massive cyber conflict, or are military networks too vulnerable to basic commercial hacking?

October 29, 2007. Kajaki, southern Afghanistan.

Major Jeffrey R. Calero was an elite Special Forces detachment commander with Company C, 1st Battalion, 20th Special Forces Group (Airborne).

Originally from Puerto Rico and raised in New York, Calero was brilliant and driven. He earned his mechanical engineering degree from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI) before choosing a life of service, earning his Green Beret in 2001.

As an officer, Calero believed in leading from the front. He never asked his men to take a step he wouldn't take first.

On October 29, 2007, while leading an Operational Detachment Alpha (ODA 2132) on a high-risk dismounted combat patrol through hostile terrain in Kajaki, an improvised explosive device (IED) was triggered.

Major Calero was killed in action, giving his life in defense of his team and his country. He was 34 years old.

Awarded the Bronze Star Medal and Purple Heart, Major Calero represented the highest standard of leadership, quiet professionalism, and selfless sacrifice within the Special Forces brotherhood.

A leader walks ahead of his men. A hero lives on in their hearts forever.

March 4, 2002. A 10,000-foot freezing mountain peak in eastern Afghanistan: Takur Ghar.

When a Navy SEAL was thrown from a damaged Chinook into an enemy hornets' nest, Air Force Combat Controller John Chapman volunteered to go back onto that mountain to get his brother back.

As soon as their helicopter touched down, they were hit with RPGs and heavy machine-gun fire. Chapman charged uphill alone through thigh-deep snow, assaulted an al-Qaeda bunker, and neutralized the fighters inside.

While assaulting a second bunker, he was shot multiple times and knocked unconscious. Believed to be fallen, his team was forced to break contact down the mountain.

But John Chapman wasn’t dead.

Sixteen years later, declassified high-definition drone footage revealed the truth: Chapman woke up alone on that freezing peak. Severely wounded and surrounded by dozens of enemy fighters, he refused to quit.

For over an hour, he fought a solo one-man stand from a snow bunker.

When an inbound quick-reaction helicopter carrying 18 Army Rangers flew directly into the ambush zone, Chapman knew they would be shredded.

He made his final choice: he stepped out of his bunker into the open, drawing all enemy fire toward himself to protect the landing helicopter until he was mortally wounded.

His solo stand saved the lives of every man on that incoming bird.

In 2018, Master Sergeant John Chapman was posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor—the first Air Force special operator to receive it since Vietnam.

Greater love hath no man than this.

On February 1, 1943, a B-17 Flying Fortress named the All American did something a plane simply isn't supposed to survive: it was cut nearly in half in mid-air, and flew home anyway.

Coming off a raid on the German-held Tunisian coast, the All American was struck when a German Messerschmitt fighter, diving in to attack, failed to pull up in time and slammed into its tail at full speed. The collision sheared through the fuselage and nearly cut the plane in two, just behind the radio compartment. The entire tail section was left hanging on by a few thin metal strips, twisting in the wind as if it might snap off at any second. By every rule of physics, the plane should have broken apart. It didn't.

The pilot, Lt. Kendrick Bragg, nursed the shattered aircraft home with the gentlest possible touch, the crew using parachute harnesses and debris to help hold the tail on. Not one man aboard had been killed or even seriously hurt. They chose to fly it home rather than bail out, limped back across North Africa, and landed. Every single man walked away alive. It remains one of the greatest testaments ever to the toughness of the B-17, the plane that brought its crews home.

The best kind of bruise a man could ever earn.

This illustration shows the kind of concealed sniper positions the Viet Cong used throughout the Vietnam War. Often called "spider holes," these were small, one man fighting positions dug into the ground, covered with a camouflaged lid made of wood, leaves, and soil, so they blended almost perfectly into the surrounding terrain.

A sniper could wait inside for hours, lift the cover just enough to take a shot, and then disappear again before anyone could locate where the fire had come from. Some positions were connected to tunnel networks, allowing the shooter to move away underground while American troops searched the area above.

For U.S. and allied forces, the threat shaped how they patrolled. Every clearing, trail, and tree line had the potential to hide a shooter who could not be seen until it was too late. It was a simple, low tech solution that proved deadly effective against a far better equipped enemy.
